title: Selection, Projection, and Rename in Relational Algebra

blocks.text: Imagine you have a massive dataset, but you're only interested in specific rows and columns. How do you efficiently extract just what you need?

blocks.markdown: In relational algebra, **selection** and **projection** are fundamental operations that allow us to filter and reshape data. Understanding these operations is crucial for querying databases effectively.

blocks.title: Selection
blocks.text: Selection (σ) is an operation in relational algebra that retrieves rows from a relation that satisfy a given predicate.

blocks.caption: Selection operation on relation R with a specified condition.

blocks.markdown: The selection operation is akin to applying a filter to a dataset. For example, if you have a table of employees and you want to find all employees in the 'Sales' department, you would use a selection operation with the condition `Department = 'Sales'`.

blocks.title: Projection
blocks.text: Projection (π) is an operation in relational algebra that retrieves specific columns from a relation, potentially removing duplicates.

blocks.caption: Projection operation on relation R selecting specified columns.

blocks.markdown: Projection is useful when you are only interested in certain attributes of a relation. For instance, if you need only the names and salaries of employees, you would project those two columns.

blocks.title: Duplicate Removal in Projection
blocks.text: Projection can result in fewer tuples than the input relation because it removes duplicate rows in the selected columns.

blocks.title: Example of Selection
blocks.prompt: Consider a relation `Employee(Name, Age, Department)` and you want to select employees who are older than 30.

steps.text: Identify the condition for selection: Age > 30.

blocks.answer: The result is a subset of the Employee relation containing only those rows where the Age attribute is greater than 30.

blocks.title: Example of Projection
blocks.prompt: Consider a relation `Employee(Name, Age, Department)` and you want to project the `Name` and `Department` columns.

steps.text: Identify the columns to project: Name, Department.

blocks.answer: The result is a relation containing only the Name and Department columns, with duplicates removed.

blocks.markdown: The **rename** operation is used to change the name of a relation or its attributes, which can be useful for clarity or when combining relations.

blocks.title: Rename
blocks.text: Rename (ρ) is an operation that assigns a new name to a relation or its attributes.

points: Selection filters rows based on a condition.
Projection selects specific columns and removes duplicates.
Rename changes the names of relations or attributes.
